# --instructions--

Write a validator using everything from this chapter:
- give `FormError` a second case `tooLong` carrying a `maximum` of type `Int`
- `validate` throws `FormError.empty` when the name is empty, throws `FormError.tooLong(maximum: 10)` when it is longer than 10 characters, and otherwise returns the name
- `safeName` returns the validated name, or `"guest"` when `validate` throws

Example of function call:
```swift
print(safeName(""))
// prints guest
```

# --before-asserts--

```swift
func _kind(_ name: String) -> String {
    do {
        return try validate(name)
    } catch FormError.empty {
        return "empty"
    } catch FormError.tooLong(let maximum) {
        return "max \(maximum)"
    } catch {
        return "other"
    }
}
```

# --asserts--

`validate("Ada")` must return `Ada`

```swift
tryCatch(_kind("Ada") == "Ada")
```

`validate("")` must throw `empty`

```swift
tryCatch(_kind("") == "empty")
```

`validate("12345678901")` must throw `tooLong` carrying `10`

```swift
tryCatch(_kind("12345678901") == "max 10")
```

a name of exactly 10 characters must be accepted

```swift
tryCatch(_kind("1234567890") == "1234567890")
```

```swift
tryCatch(safeName("Ada") == "Ada")
```

`safeName("12345678901")` must return `guest`


# --solutions--

```swift
enum FormError: Error {
    case empty
    case tooLong(maximum: Int)
}

func validate(_ name: String) throws -> String {
    guard !name.isEmpty else {
        throw FormError.empty
    }
    guard name.count <= 10 else {
        throw FormError.tooLong(maximum: 10)
    }
    return name
}

func safeName(_ name: String) -> String {
    return (try? validate(name)) ?? "guest"
}
```
